# FileShed

> FileShed is a retired Open WebUI add-on for agentic work: command-driven operations, data pipelines, document and media transformations, precise editing, Git-versioned documents, group collaboration and authenticated deliverables. Persistent storage is one foundation, not its full scope.

Status: **Retired**. The author, Fade78, stopped active development when Open WebUI OpenTerminal covered much of his own workflow. The project remains available for its implementation and design ideas; this is not a current compatibility or maintenance promise.

Use FileShed's documentation for its Open WebUI tool-calling interface. Use Pasteberth for artifact staging between tools, or LightWebPres to publish Markdown as readable pages and presentations: they are different projects, not interchangeable implementations.

The documented workflow combines `shed_exec`, SQLite, CSV export, ZIP creation and authenticated download links. External commands must be installed; network access is disabled by default. Documents and Groups use automatic Git history, unlike every file in Storage. Application safeguards are not an OS sandbox. Personal encryption has documented limits.

The source snapshot declares 1.1.0 and 44 public `shed_*` methods; the README and historical reports describe 1.0.5 and 38 functions. Read the source notes before relying on a version-specific feature or historical test result.

## Start here

- [Product overview](https://fadeshed.github.io/fileshed/overview.md): capabilities, workspace contexts, workflow, source versions and security boundaries.
- [Original guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Fade78/Fileshed/e69757ccab2aed5ce19dd615ffa2d86b16a08ba9/README.md): installation in Open WebUI, Native Function Calling, examples and function reference.
- [Design specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Fade78/Fileshed/e69757ccab2aed5ce19dd615ffa2d86b16a08ba9/docs/SPEC.md): layered architecture, groups, permissions, help, locking and encryption.
